note: One entry per relationship type. All edges are directed and originate at a Document node. Each edge is derived from exactly one metadata field, so the edge set is reproducible from the corpus alone. Phase 2 adds five MENTIONS_* relationships (Document -> concept, carrying the matched trigger and evidence text) and three Service-anchored co-occurrence relationships marked confidence='cooccurrence'.

BELONGS_TO_CATEGORY.meaning: This document is filed under this NovaTel business category. Exactly one per document; the backbone of topical navigation in the graph.

IS_TYPE.meaning: This document has this editorial form (FAQ, SOP, RCA, Policy and so on). Lets a retriever prefer procedural SOPs over conversational transcripts for a how-to question.

OWNED_BY_DEPARTMENT.meaning: This department is the internal owner and authority for the document. Supports ownership and routing questions such as which team owns fraud policy.

APPLIES_TO_SCOPE.meaning: This document applies to this customer segment. Enables segment-correct answers so a prepaid customer is not shown a postpaid-only policy.

HAS_TAG.meaning: This document carries this keyword. One edge per tag, so a document with three tags produces three edges. Tags are the densest cross-category connector in the graph.

AUTHORED_BY.meaning: This authority published or vouches for the document. Currently a single-valued field, kept as a first-class relationship because provenance and trust weighting will need it once external sources are ingested.

PART_OF_DATASET.meaning: This document belongs to this corpus, derived from the document_id prefix. Keeps benchmark data (SciFact) separable from NovaTel operational content in every downstream query.

RELATED_TO.meaning: The source document declares the target as a related read. The only document-to-document relationship in Phase 1. Targets that do not exist among the 148 canonical documents are preserved as stub Document nodes with resolved=false rather than being dropped, so the unresolved rate stays measurable.

MENTIONS_SERVICE.meaning: The document text names this service. Carries the trigger phrases that fired and a snippet of the surrounding text, so the claim is auditable.
MENTIONS_SERVICE.cardinality: 0..n per document, one edge per distinct concept

MENTIONS_CHANNEL.meaning: The document text names this delivery channel. Answers 'what can a customer do in the app' without reading the documents.
MENTIONS_CHANNEL.cardinality: 0..n per document, one edge per distinct concept

MENTIONS_VERIFICATION.meaning: The document text names this identity-verification mechanism. Useful for impact analysis, e.g. every document affected by an OTP outage.
MENTIONS_VERIFICATION.cardinality: 0..n per document, one edge per distinct concept

MENTIONS_REQUIREMENT.meaning: The document text names this as something the customer must produce.
MENTIONS_REQUIREMENT.cardinality: 0..n per document, one edge per distinct concept

MENTIONS_LOCATION.meaning: The document text directs the customer to this physical place, i.e. the journey cannot be completed digitally.
MENTIONS_LOCATION.cardinality: 0..n per document, one edge per distinct concept

AVAILABLE_VIA.meaning: The service and the channel are mentioned in the same document, suggesting the service can be reached through that channel.
AVAILABLE_VIA.cardinality: 0..n, aggregated so one pair is one edge
AVAILABLE_VIA.caveat: Heuristic, not an asserted fact. Same-document co-mention is weak evidence: a policy document listing every channel produces pairs no one intended. Read 'support' (how many documents back the pair) before trusting an edge.

REQUIRES_VERIFICATION.meaning: The service and the verification method are mentioned in the same document, suggesting the service is gated on that method.
REQUIRES_VERIFICATION.cardinality: 0..n, aggregated so one pair is one edge
REQUIRES_VERIFICATION.caveat: Heuristic, not an asserted fact. Same-document co-mention is weak evidence: a policy document listing every channel produces pairs no one intended. Read 'support' (how many documents back the pair) before trusting an edge.

REQUIRES_DOCUMENT.meaning: The service and the requirement are mentioned in the same document, suggesting the customer must produce it to complete the service.
REQUIRES_DOCUMENT.cardinality: 0..n, aggregated so one pair is one edge
REQUIRES_DOCUMENT.caveat: Heuristic, not an asserted fact. Same-document co-mention is weak evidence: a policy document listing every channel produces pairs no one intended. Read 'support' (how many documents back the pair) before trusting an edge.

OF_CUSTOMER.meaning: This row belongs to this customer. Aggregates the customer_id FK of all 14 referencing tables into one relationship, so 'everything about this customer' is a single hop instead of fourteen joins.
OF_CUSTOMER.integrity: Every edge is written only after the FK value is checked against the parent table's real primary-key set. Measured integrity is 1.0 with 0 dangling.

FOR_PLAN.integrity: Every edge is written only after the FK value is checked against the parent table's real primary-key set. Measured integrity is 1.0 with 0 dangling.

IN_CATEGORY.meaning: Schema-view only: an entity type belongs to a structured category code. Never join this to the document branch's Category nodes - see the crosswalk warning.

REALIZES_CONCEPT.meaning: This structured table realizes this business concept. Deterministic: read straight from the Phase 4 crosswalk, one edge per crosswalk row.

EXPRESSES_CONCEPT.meaning: This document category or extracted service expresses this business concept. Both mappings are explicit tables - no fuzzy or string matching is used anywhere in the bridge.

INSTANCE_OF.source_field: entity_type property of the instance node
INSTANCE_OF.meaning: A database row is an instance of its EntityType. This is what carries the bridge down from the schema node to the 43,928 real rows; without it, Document -> Concept -> EntityType stops at the type and never reaches a Customer.
INSTANCE_OF.cost_note: One edge per row. It is the largest single relationship type in the database - load it deliberately, and skip it with --no-instance-of if only schema-level bridging is wanted.
